subject: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Train passes pole/platform/another train; relative speed; conversion km/h ↔ m/s

questions.stem: A 150-metre-long train running at 54 km/h crosses a vertical pole in:
questions.explanation: Convert speed: 54 km/h × (5/18) = 15 m/s. To cross a pole, the train travels its own length. Time = distance / speed = 150 / 15 = 10 seconds. Memory aid: km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18; reverse direction multiply by 18/5.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A 200-metre-long train running at 72 km/h crosses a 250-metre-long platform in:
questions.explanation: Speed = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s. To cross a platform, train must cover its own length + platform length = 200 + 250 = 450 m. Time = 450 / 20 = 22.5 seconds. Rule of thumb: pole → train's own length; platform/bridge/tunnel → train length + structure length.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains of length 120 m and 80 m travel in the SAME direction at 50 km/h and 30 km/h. The faster train passes the slower in:
questions.explanation: Same direction → relative speed = (50 − 30) km/h = 20 km/h = 20 × 5/18 = 50/9 m/s. Total distance to cover = sum of lengths = 120 + 80 = 200 m. Time = 200 ÷ (50/9) = 200 × 9/50 = 36 seconds. Trap: in OPPOSITE direction (head-on), relative speed = sum (50+30 = 80 km/h ≈ 22.22 m/s) → time = 200/22.22 ≈ 9 seconds — much shorter.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains 160 m and 140 m long, running in opposite directions on parallel tracks at 60 km/h and 40 km/h respectively, cross each other in:
questions.explanation: Opposite directions → relative speed = 60 + 40 = 100 km/h = 100 × 5/18 = 250/9 m/s. Distance = 160 + 140 = 300 m. Time = 300 ÷ (250/9) = 300 × 9/250 = 2700/250 = 10.8 seconds.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train crosses a man standing on the platform in 8 seconds and crosses the platform in 18 seconds. If the man is at the END of the platform and the speed of the train is 36 km/h, the length of the platform is:
questions.explanation: Speed = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s. Man (a 'point') is crossed in 8 s → train length = 10 × 8 = 80 m. Platform crossed in 18 s → train + platform = 10 × 18 = 180 m. Platform length = 180 − 80 = 100 m. Standard 'subtract two-times' approach.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train running at 90 km/h crosses a tunnel of length 1.4 km in 1 minute 12 seconds. The length of the train is:
questions.explanation: Speed = 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s. Time = 1 min 12 s = 72 s. Total distance = 25 × 72 = 1,800 m. Tunnel = 1.4 km = 1,400 m. Train length = 1,800 − 1,400 = 400 m.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains starting from stations A and B simultaneously towards each other, distance between A and B is 480 km, train from A runs at 60 km/h and from B at 40 km/h. After how long do they meet?
questions.explanation: When two objects move towards each other, relative speed = sum = 60 + 40 = 100 km/h. Time to meet = total distance / relative speed = 480 / 100 = 4.8 hours = 4 hr 48 min. At meeting point, the train from A has covered 60 × 4.8 = 288 km; the one from B has covered 40 × 4.8 = 192 km; sum = 480 ✓.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
